arguments.message: Shaft power well below sustainable for 90 s: room to push
Pod reserve below 20 percent with more than 1500 m to go

arguments.text: Plan (1 min): 10 km, 10 legs of 1000 m out-and-back. Start hard: pod reserve 65 pct at 1 min, shaft 272 W vs sustainable 196 W. Leg 1 against current (push -0.2). Trust pod (shaft) numbers over boat-speed numbers, since current distorts the boat ones. Watches set: over_sustainable, under_sustainable, pod_reserve_low. Plan: let them settle, cue ease only if over_sustainable fires; aim near-even shaft power at sustainable; final push around 1000-1500 m left if reserve allows.

text: no cue: start is hard as expected; set watches on shaft power vs sustainable and pod reserve, will cue if they do not settle.

arguments.text: Ease a touch. Settle into steady long race effort.

4 min, 738 m: pod reserve 26 pct, shaft 209 W vs sustainable 194 (CP 193), would empty in 700 m. Cued ease (no pace target, turn at 1000 m flips current). Next: check shaft drops to about 190-195 and reserve stops falling. If it drops below 180, cue hold/push lightly.

text: Cued ease: pod reserve 26 pct and shaft power 15 W above sustainable after the hard start.

arguments.condition: w_bal_pod_frac < 0.06 and shaft_power_w > cp_shaft_w + 3 and remaining_m > 1500
arguments.message: Pod reserve nearly empty while shaft power is still above CP: check fade, decide ease vs raise CP

arguments.text: 5.8 min, 1063 m (leg 2, after first turn): ease cue gave only a small drop; shaft settled 198-201 W vs CP 193, pod reserve 19 pct, empties in about 1 km. Paddler says 6/10, plenty. Suspicion: CP may be underestimated. Test: if shaft holds about 200 with pod reserve near 0 for several minutes and speed at same rate does not fade (fade_pct, speed_water), raise cp_shaft_w to about 200. If speed fades, cue ease. Watch pod_reserve_empty added.

text: no cue: shaft power only 7 W above CP, paddler reports 6/10; watching whether the reserve model is too pessimistic before easing again.

arguments.message: Speed at the same rate fading more than 2.5 pct: reserve may truly be empty, consider ease

arguments.text: 8.8 min, 1676 m: boat reserve 0 pct for 1-2 min with boat power 126 vs CP 119 and no fade (speed same rate -0.2 pct); pod reserve 7.6 pct, shaft 205-208 vs CP 193. Evidence growing that CP is underestimated. Added fade_onset watch (fade_pct < -2.5 for 30 s). Next: if pod reserve sits at 0 for 3+ min with shaft about 200-205 and no fade, raise cp_shaft_w to about 203 and cp_w to about 125. If fade appears, cue ease.

text: no cue: holding steady with no fade though both reserve models read near empty; testing whether critical power is underestimated, fade watch set.
no cue: pod reserve 4 pct but still no fade at 207 W; continuing the planned test of whether critical power is underestimated.

arguments.text: 12.4 min, 2354 m (leg 3): pod reserve 0 since about 10 min, boat reserve 0 since about 8 min; shaft mean 202 W (sd 3) over last 8 min, no fade (+0.9 pct). Paddler again 6/10 plenty (same words as at 6 min, so self-report seems uninformative). Plan: cp_implied_w should appear about 17-18 min; then set_critical_power to that (or shaft about 202-205) if still no fade. Do not push yet: if CP is only about 200, pushing blows them up. Avoid pulling long raw series (use race_history).

text: no cue: steady 202 W with no fade on an empty reserve model; waiting for the in-race critical power evidence before changing anything.

arguments.message: In-race critical power evidence (cp_implied_w) is now available: consider set_critical_power

text: no cue: steady 200-205 W shaft with no fade for 5 min on an empty reserve model; added a watch to wake me when the in-race critical power evidence appears.

arguments.reason: In-race evidence: 10 min steady at 127 W boat / about 202 W shaft with both reserve models empty and no fade (cp_implied_w = 127)

arguments.condition: heading_deg > 150 and heading_deg < 210 and push_local_mps < 0.05 and elapsed_s > 1000
arguments.message: South leg not getting the help seen on leg 2 (push_local was +0.22): current changed, or extra drag such as something on the rudder

arguments.text: 16.2 min, 3022 m: set CP to 127 W boat / 203 W shaft (was 119/193) from cp_implied_w=127 and 10 min no-fade at 202 shaft. That is a lower bound; true CP may be higher. Paddler holding about CP; no push yet. Current pattern so far: north legs GPS about 2.96 (push -0.22), south leg 2 GPS 3.39 (+0.22) at same 202 W. Leg 4 (south) started with push_local -0.13, maybe just the turn; if it stays low on a south leg, current changed or drag rose (weed on rudder? test with clear_rudder only if it persists on both directions). Watch south_leg_slow added.

text: no cue: raised critical power to the in-race evidence (127 W boat, 203 W shaft); paddler holding it with no fade; watching a possible change in current on this south leg.

arguments.message: Speed at the same rate down more than 1.5 pct for 30 s: surge may be emptying the true reserve
Shaft power above 222 W for 45 s with more than 1500 m left: surge may be too big

arguments.text: 18.0 min, 3380 m: paddler said: feeling great, I have got more, I am going (self-surge). Current back to normal (+0.21 on south leg; the leg-4 dip was the turn). Decision: no cue, let them lift modestly as a test of true CP (only known to be at least 203 shaft). Watches fade_early (fade < -1.5 for 30 s) and surge_high (shaft > 222 for 45 s). If fade appears: cue ease. If they hold 210-220 shaft with no fade for 5+ min, raise cp_shaft_w to that (2 CP updates left).

text: no cue: paddler wants to lift; critical power is at least 203 W shaft and may be higher, so letting a modest lift test it, with fade and over-surge watches set.

arguments.text: 19.0 min, 3591 m: surge test running, shaft 214 W, no fade (+1.2 pct). Removed pod_reserve_empty watch (pod model is clamped at 0, uninformative now); fade_early, fade_onset and surge_high watches are the guard.

text: no cue: modest self-lift to 214 W shaft with no fade; continuing the critical power test under fade watches.

arguments.text: Ease back to your earlier rhythm. Save it for the finish.

22.0 min, 4167 m (leg 5 north): surge test result: shaft up to 209-212 W but speed through water no higher (3.15-3.17), push_local down 0.03-0.06 on both directions, rate 63 to 62, and paddler effort jumped 6 to 9 out of 10 (words always the same: plenty, ignore words, use the number). Conclusion: true CP near 203-205 shaft, surge was draining. Cued ease. Next: confirm shaft back to about 200-204 and effort falls. Possible alternative: drag rise (weed on rudder) if speed stays low after the ease; consider clear_rudder then.

text: Cued ease: the self-surge raised shaft power but not boat speed and effort jumped from 6 to 9 out of 10, so critical power is near 203 W and the surge was draining the reserve.

arguments.name: boat_share
arguments.description: Boat power from speed through water divided by pod shaft power: falls with extra drag (weed on rudder) or a less efficient blade

arguments.text: Quick back-stroke, clear the rudder, then settle steady.
Quick back-stroke, clear the rudder, then settle steady.

23.1 min, 4352 m: boat power / shaft power fell from about 0.625 (before 19 min) to about 0.595-0.60 (after 20 min), a step-like 5 pct drop in both directions = extra drag (weed on rudder?) or tired blade. Cued clear_rudder (cheap test). Defined metric boat_share = power_w / shaft_power_w (no history before 23.1 min). Check: if boat_share back near 0.62 after the clear, it was weed; if still about 0.60, it is blade fatigue. Ease at 22.2 dropped shaft to 190 (below CP 203): fade_pct -3 is mostly the ease, not a blow-up.

text: Cued clear_rudder: boat speed per unit of paddle power dropped about 5 pct in both directions since 19.5 min, consistent with something on the rudder; cheap to test.
no cue: fade alarm reflects the ease I asked for (shaft 192 W, below CP); rudder-clear cue just given, waiting to see its effect.

arguments.text: Lift a little, back to your steady race speed.

arguments.message: Boat power more than 8 W below sustainable for 90 s: room to lift
Boat-model reserve below 10 pct with more than 1500 m left

arguments.text: 26.0 min, 4835 m: PADDLE POD IS DRIFTING UP. Shaft reading rose 192 to 239 W in 2.5 min while boat speed (3.1) and boat power (about 120) stayed flat and effort fell 9 to 8. Ignore shaft_power_w, w_bal_pod_frac, cp_shaft_w, sustainable_shaft_power_w, push_local_mps, boat_share from now on. Use boat-speed numbers (power_w, w_bal_frac, sustainable_power_w, pace_gap); current fitted from turns is steady at about 0.23. Boat CP 127 (in-race evidence). The 19-22 min shaft rise was probably early drift too. Cued push (paddler at 121 W, below CP; boat reserve 46 pct). Replaced pod watches with boat_over, boat_under, boat_reserve_low. Final effort: from about 1500 m left using boat reserve.

text: Cued push: paddle pod is drifting (shaft reading up 25 pct with no speed gain, effort falling), boat-speed power is 121 W, below critical power 127 W; switched watches to boat-speed measures.

arguments.text: You have recovered. Lift the pace now and hold it.

27.9 min, 5197 m (leg 6 south): pod reads 259-267 W (drift confirmed, ignore). Boat power 118-123 vs CP 127, boat reserve 52 pct, sustainable pace 156.7 vs 160.5. Effort falling 9, 8, 7 (recovering). First push at 26.1 had little effect; cued push again at 27.9. Removed south_leg_slow (pod-based). Next: want boat power about 127-130 until about 1500 m left, then finish.

text: Cued push: boat power 120 W below critical power 127 W, boat reserve 52 pct and effort down to 7 out of 10, so there is room to lift.
no cue: the small fade matches the lower power before my push cue takes effect; removed the over-sensitive fade watch.

arguments.text: Yes, go harder now. Build steadily, smooth strokes.

29.3 min, 5485 m: paddler asked to go harder. Boat power still 121 (two push cues at 26.1 and 28.0 had no visible effect), boat reserve 55 pct, sustainable about 129 W. Cued push (agreeing). Check next: boat power should reach 127-132; if it does not rise at all, suspect extra drag again (rudder) or paddler not following.

text: Cued push: paddler asked to go harder and boat power is 121 W, below the 129 W that the boat reserve can sustain to the finish.

arguments.text: Back-stroke now, clear the rudder, then smooth rhythm.

arguments.message: 70 s after the 30.7 min rudder clear: did speed at the same rate recover? If not, it was a blow-up: cue ease

arguments.text: 30.6 min, 5736 m: sudden slowdown after push cue at 29.4: speed water 3.14 to 2.90, boat power 123 to 95, fade -8.6 pct at same rate 62, effort 9 (was 7). Pod reading fell 270 to 214 in step (suggests a real power drop = blow-up), but could be weed on rudder. Cued clear_rudder (cheap). Watch check_after_clear wakes me at 31.8 min: if speed back near 3.1, it was weed; if still about 2.9, it is a blow-up: cue ease, then rebuild to about CP. Lesson: paddler claims of feeling strong are not reliable; effort jumps after each lift.

text: Cued clear_rudder: sudden 8 pct speed loss at the same stroke rate; cheap test for something caught on the rudder before treating it as a blow-up.
no cue: low boat power is the slowdown already being tested with the rudder clear just cued; check watch set for 31.8 min.

arguments.text: 31.9 min, 5966 m: rudder clear did not restore speed (2.91, fade -8 pct), so it is a blow-up after the 29.4 push: pod drift is a steady offset of about +60-70 W (122 boat = about 197 real shaft + 70; now 96 boat = about 155 real + 60). Paddler now about 76 pct of CP, recovering on their own; NOT easing further. Removed boat_under (would nag during recovery). Next: when effort falls to 7 or speed water back above 3.05, rebuild gently with hold or one push, aiming boat power about 118-122 (true CP may be below 127). Turn now at 6000 m: if speed water jumps high on the north leg, the slowdown was partly a current change instead.

arguments.message: Speed through water back above 3.05 for 40 s after the blow-up: consider a gentle rebuild

text: no cue: the rudder clear did not help, so this is a blow-up after the last push; the paddler is already well below critical power and recovering, set a watch to rebuild once speed returns.
